# aether_node_pool (Resource)

A pool of identically sized worker nodes in an `aether_cluster`. A pool is FIXED (billed as a flat monthly fee, `desired_nodes` nodes) unless its budget allows growth (a `max_vcpus` above `min_vcpus` or a `max_memory_gb` above `min_memory_gb`), which makes it AUTOSCALING (billed hourly per node, node count chosen by the autoscaler inside the budget). Creation waits until the pool is `running`. On update, only a node-count change on a fixed pool is waited for (until every desired node is ready); every other change returns once the API has accepted it, because the platform exposes no signal that it has been applied.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "cluster_id" {
  type = string
}

# Fixed pool: billed as a flat monthly fee; apply waits until desired_nodes nodes are ready.
# vcpus, memory_gb, disk_gb and name REPLACE the pool when changed.
resource "aether_node_pool" "workers" {
  cluster_id            = var.cluster_id
  name                  = "workers"
  vcpus                 = 4
  memory_gb             = 16
  disk_gb               = 80
  desired_nodes         = 3
  drain_timeout_seconds = 600 # once set it cannot be removed, only changed

  node_labels = {
    "team" = "platform"
  }
}

# Autoscaling pool: max_vcpus above min_vcpus (or max_memory_gb above min_memory_gb) makes it
# autoscaling, billed hourly per node; the autoscaler picks the node count inside the budget.
resource "aether_node_pool" "batch" {
  cluster_id    = var.cluster_id
  name          = "batch"
  vcpus         = 8
  memory_gb     = 32
  disk_gb       = 100
  min_vcpus     = 8
  max_vcpus     = 64
  min_memory_gb = 32
  max_memory_gb = 256

  scale_down_delay_seconds       = 900
  scale_down_utilization_percent = 40

  node_taints = [{
    key    = "workload"
    value  = "batch"
    effect = "NoSchedule" # a NoSchedule taint needs another untainted pool in the cluster
  }]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) UUID of the `aether_cluster` the pool belongs to. Changing it replaces the pool.
- `disk_gb` (Number) Disk per node in GB (1-2048). Changing it REPLACES the pool, for the same reason as `vcpus`.
- `memory_gb` (Number) Memory per node in GB (1-512). Changing it REPLACES the pool, for the same reason as `vcpus`.
- `name` (String) Pool name (lowercase letters, digits and `-`, at most 40 characters). Changing it REPLACES the pool: the platform would destroy and recreate every node on a rename anyway, so the plan says so. The old pool is deleted before the new one is created, because a pool keeps its name until its deletion completes. Under `lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true }` a same-name replacement (e.g. a `vcpus`/`memory_gb`/`disk_gb` change) fails with the API's 409 "Node pool already exists", because the old pool is still LIVE (not yet deleted) and still holds its name when the new one's create runs.
- `vcpus` (Number) vCPUs per node (1-128). Changing it REPLACES the pool: the platform never applies a size change to any existing or future node of a pool, so only a new pool gets the new size.

### Optional

- `desired_nodes` (Number) Number of nodes. Defaults to 1 at create. On a fixed pool a change scales the pool, and apply waits until that many nodes are ready. On an AUTOSCALING pool it only seeds the initial size: after create the platform ignores it (the autoscaler owns the node count), so changing it is stored but changes nothing.
- `drain_timeout_seconds` (Number) How long a node being removed may take to drain, 30-3600 seconds. Omit it to track the platform default (currently 600). **Once set it cannot be removed**: the API has no way to clear it, so removing it from the configuration is refused at plan time. Set an explicit value instead (e.g. `600`), or recreate the pool: taint it (`terraform taint`/`tofu taint`) then apply with the attribute removed - `-replace` and `replace_triggered_by` hit the same refusal and do not work here.
- `max_memory_gb` (Number) Autoscaling budget: maximum total memory of the pool in GB (at least `memory_gb` when set). `0` (the default) means no budget; see `min_vcpus`. Removing the attribute sets it back to `0`.
- `max_nodes` (Number) Upper node bound. When omitted it follows `desired_nodes`. The platform derives an autoscaling pool's real bounds from its budget, not from this value.
- `max_vcpus` (Number) Autoscaling budget: maximum total vCPUs of the pool (at least `vcpus` when set). `0` (the default) means no budget; see `min_vcpus`. Removing the attribute sets it back to `0`.
- `min_memory_gb` (Number) Autoscaling budget: minimum total memory of the pool in GB. `0` (the default) means no budget; see `min_vcpus`. Removing the attribute sets it back to `0`.
- `min_nodes` (Number) Lower node bound, `min_nodes <= desired_nodes <= max_nodes`. When omitted it follows `desired_nodes`. The platform derives an autoscaling pool's real bounds from its budget, not from this value.
- `min_vcpus` (Number) Autoscaling budget: minimum total vCPUs of the pool. `0` (the default) means no budget. All four budget attributes at `0` make a FIXED pool, billed as a flat monthly fee; a `max_vcpus` above `min_vcpus` (or `max_memory_gb` above `min_memory_gb`) makes the pool AUTOSCALING, billed hourly per node. A non-zero minimum must cover at least one node. Removing the attribute sets it back to `0`.
- `node_labels` (Map of String) Kubernetes labels applied to every node. Keys under `aether.cloud/`, `kubernetes.io/`, `k8s.io/`, `node-role.kubernetes.io/` and `node.kubernetes.io/` are reserved. Immutable: changing them replaces the pool.
- `node_taints` (Attributes List) Kubernetes taints applied to every node. A `NoSchedule` or `NoExecute` taint needs another untainted pool in the cluster. Immutable: changing them replaces the pool. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--node_taints))
- `scale_down_delay_seconds` (Number) Autoscaling: how long a node must be unneeded before it is removed, 60-3600 seconds. Omit it for the platform default (currently 600). Once set, the API cannot clear it: removing it from the configuration keeps the stored value.
- `scale_down_utilization_percent` (Number) Autoscaling: utilization below which a node counts as unneeded, 10-90 percent. Omit it for the platform default (currently 50). Once set, the API cannot clear it: removing it from the configuration keeps the stored value.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation time (RFC 3339).
- `current_nodes` (Number) Number of ready nodes the platform reports. On an autoscaling pool it moves with the autoscaler, which is not drift.
- `first_ready_at` (String) Time the pool first had a ready node (RFC 3339); null until then.
- `id` (String) Node pool UUID.
- `status` (String) Lifecycle status reported by the API: `provisioning`, `running`, `scaling`, `scaling-down`, `degraded` (with `status_message`; clears by itself once the nodes recover) or `deleting`.
- `status_message` (String) Explanation accompanying a `degraded` status.
- `updated_at` (String) Last update time (RFC 3339). The platform moves it without any API call.

Required:

- `effect` (String) `NoSchedule`, `PreferNoSchedule` or `NoExecute`.
- `key` (String) Taint key.

- `value` (String) Taint value; defaults to empty.


<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
